hints.content: To translate quadrilateral $ABCD$ using $(x,y)\to(x -7,y +1)$, we basically translate quadrilateral $ABCD$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD{C(5,-2)}$ is translated to $(5 -7,-2 +1)=\greenD{(-2,-1)}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at six, negative five, B at zero, negative three, C at five, negative two, and D at five, negative four. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves seven units left from vertex C and up one unit to a point at negative two, negative one.

hints.content:
Doing this for all vertices and connecting them, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a quadrilateral having vertices A at six, negative five, B at zero, negative three, C at five, negative two, and D at five, negative four. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves seven units left from the four vertices and up one unit to a form an image of a congruent quadrilateral with vertices at negative two, negative one, negative two, negative three, negative one, negative four, and negative seven, negative two.

question.content:
